title: Run correspondence for the silent simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $m$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ satisfies: if the input-head position of $c$ is $0$, then $b=\mathrm{false}$, and if that position is $|y|+1$, then $b=\mathrm{true}$. For any Boolean word $x$, any input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, any Boolean lists $u$ and $v$, and any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a Boolean tag $b'$ satisfying the same boundary conditions for the input-head position of the configuration reached from $c$ after $t$ steps, such that running the silent simulation for $t$ steps from the corresponding encoded configuration gives exactly the encoded configuration of that $t$-step run, with tag $b'$ and the same $p,u,v$.
